title: Probing-stepper autoscaler with backpressure-aware KV-cache affinity and rollback windows
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design and implement a new autoscaling algorithm for Dedicated fleets that performs small, controlled probing steps while preserving KV-cache affinity for session-sensitive workloads and supporting deterministic rollback windows. The goal is to hit tenant throughput guarantees with minimal tail-latency regressions and bounded cost exposure. This ticket covers metric selection, probing and stepper algorithm, affinity-aware placement hints, and safety envelopes (max step, cooldown, emergency cap, rollback criteria).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Autoscaler performs incremental probes (<= 10% capacity steps) and either keeps the step or automatically rollbacks within a configurable rollback window when tail latency or error rate breaches thresholds. 2) New placement hints preserve KV-cache affinity for at least 70% of sessions during scale events in canary traffic. 3) Composite target metric (throughput SLO + p99 completion latency) is computed and used to trigger scale actions. 4) Safety limits: max step, cost budget gate, and emergency cap are enforced and audited in logs. 5) End-to-end integration tests and a production canary run demonstrate stable behavior for a representative tenant load pattern.
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Primary objective: prefer stability and SLA adherence over aggressive cost savings for committed tenants—we bias probes toward small positive steps and fast rollback when regressions seen.
Metric choice: we use a composite target (weighted sum of short-window throughput achievement and p99 completion latency) rather than raw CPU/GPU utilization to better reflect user experience.
Probing cadence: short probes (30s-2m) allow quick detection of benefits but increase noise; we add hysteresis and a moving baseline to avoid reacting to microbursts.

KV-cache affinity: packing new replicas where sessions can reuse hot KV entries reduces per-token compute; this increases placement complexity and may reduce pure packing efficiency—acceptable tradeoff for latency-sensitive workloads.
Rollback policy: we prefer proactive rollback within a tight window (configurable, default 3m) instead of gradual scale-down when regressions are detected to bound SLA violations.
Cost gating: max spend per probe is enforced via a cost budget gate; higher-tier tenants can opt-in to faster/fuller probes.

Fallbacks: when placement constraints prevent affinity-preserving placement, autoscaler will either fall back to a larger cooldown or use a warm-start strategy (pre-warm KV cache) before accepting traffic.
Complexity vs observability: algorithm adds new metrics (probe_id, affinity_score, rollback_reason) to trace events for debugging—slightly more telemetry cost but essential for postmortems.
Model-forecasting: we include a light-weight linear forecast to recommend probe magnitude; full ML predictor deferred to a follow-up ticket to reduce scope.
Safety-first: large-scale automated surge is gated behind an administrative override and must include explicit runbook steps.
Performance risk: small-step probing adds control loops that may interact with existing headroom controllers—will coordinate with ENG-4127 and ENG-47218.
Security note: placement hints and affinity metadata are treated as non-sensitive telemetry; any modifications that touch tenant secrets will require KMS integration and a separate security review.
implementation_notes:
- Implement a StepperController that accepts target composite metric and recommended step size.
- Probe lifecycle: allocate ephemeral step (tagged by probe_id) -> route a sampled fraction of traffic (1-10%) for probe window -> measure composite delta -> commit or rollback.
- Affinity hinting subsystem: add placement_hint metadata to orchestration API to prefer nodes with warm KV for tenant/session.
- Rollback detection rules: p99_completion_latency > baseline * 1.25 OR error_rate increase > 0.5pp triggers rollback.
- Safety envelopes: max_step_percent, cooldown_seconds, per-tenant_cost_budget, emergency_cap_count.
- Telemetry: emit probe_id, probe_fraction, affinity_score, metric_deltas, rollback_reason, decision_timestamp.
- Integration tests: synthetic traffic harness that simulates cache-sensitive conversational sessions and cacheless batch tokenization workloads.
- Documentation: update console rollout UI to include probe visualization and rollback audit trail.
